text: The Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees that if f is continuous on [a,b] with f(a) and f(b) of opposite sign, then f has a root in (a,b).
explanation: This is the sign-change form of the IVT, a consequence of the completeness of R. Continuity is essential: a function with a jump discontinuity can pass from negative to positive values without ever equalling zero.
